nodes.label: Development Patterns
nodes.rationale: Core and advanced patterns for Stellar smart contracts. Setup stays in SKILL.md; tests and security review are the other companions.

nodes.label: Execution Model
nodes.rationale: Contracts run as WebAssembly guests in a sandboxed host inside stellar-core. Each transaction has its own host, and each invoked contract has its own guest VM. The host meters every step. A transaction is the atomicity boundary: errors, panics, missing auth, and budget exhaustion roll back every ledger write, including nested calls. A caller can catch a callee error with try_ client methods and continue. Contract state lives in storage, never in the #[contract] struct.

nodes.label: stellar-core
nodes.rationale: The sandboxed contract host runs inside stellar-core.

nodes.label: Host Reentrancy Block
nodes.rationale: The host blocks reentrancy, direct or indirect, on normal calls. External calls are still failure, budget, and side-effect boundaries, so order state updates deliberately.

nodes.label: env.prng
nodes.rationale: env.prng() is seeded from ledger state and is predictable. Never use it for keys, auth, or high-stakes randomness.

nodes.label: Instance Storage
nodes.rationale: instance() shares one TTL with the contract instance and is archived and restorable with it. Use it for an admin, config, and other small globals. One extend_ttl warms every global, but the entry is capped at 64KB serialized on mainnet. Never put per-user or unbounded data there.

nodes.label: Persistent Storage
nodes.rationale: persistent() has a per-key TTL. Expired entries are archived and can be restored. Use it for user balances and anything that must survive. New persistent entries start with about 120 days of TTL on mainnet.

nodes.label: Temporary Storage
nodes.rationale: temporary() has a per-key TTL and is deleted permanently on expiry. Use it for caches, time-bounded data, and oracle prices. It is the cheapest storage, starts around one day of TTL, and has no restore path.

nodes.label: extend_ttl
nodes.rationale: extend_ttl(threshold, extend_to) does nothing unless the current TTL is below the threshold, then sets TTL to extend_to. It is idempotent and never shortens TTL. Extending on write makes active users pay for their own state; extending instance TTL at busy entry points keeps globals alive. Rent is charged at invocation time. No entry can exceed about 180 days (3,110,400 ledgers). A ledger is about 5 seconds (17,280 per day).

nodes.label: extend_ttl_with_limits
nodes.rationale: Protocol 26 added extend_ttl_with_limits for persistent and instance storage so callers cannot force arbitrary rent. Arguments are extend_to, min_extension, and max_extension.

nodes.label: ExtendFootprintTTLOp
nodes.rationale: Anyone can extend any entry's TTL with ExtendFootprintTTLOp and no contract auth. Keep-alive services are possible, and TTL expiry is not a security mechanism. If data must die after a deadline, store the deadline in the value and check it.

nodes.label: Automatic Archival Restore
nodes.rationale: Since protocol 23, archived persistent entries in the read-write footprint are restored automatically and storage rent is paid again. Simulation handles this. Temporary entries have no restore path. Code should still use get().unwrap_or(default) or has() where absence matters.

nodes.label: Typed Storage Keys
nodes.rationale: A #[contracttype] enum for keys centralizes the schema, prevents collisions, and grows by adding variants. Keep keys fine-grained. Transactions declare a read/write footprint up front and serialize on the same read-write entry, so fine-grained keys let unrelated calls run in parallel. A giant map makes every caller pay to read all of it.

nodes.label: Transaction Footprint
nodes.rationale: Every touched ledger entry must be in the footprint whether it is used or not. Each read or write has a fixed cost plus bytes. Minimize distinct entries.

nodes.label: i128
nodes.rationale: i128 is the canonical SEP-41 token amount. It allows negatives, so reject amount < 0 on inputs.

nodes.label: U256 and I256
nodes.rationale: 256-bit math uses U256 and I256. checked_add, sub, mul, pow, div, rem_euclid, shl, and shr return Option. Available in protocol 26 and later.

nodes.label: MuxedAddress
nodes.rationale: MuxedAddress distinguishes sub-accounts of one address for exchanges and custodians. transfer accepts it as the destination, and a plain Address converts into it.

nodes.label: Timepoint and Duration
nodes.rationale: Timepoint and Duration are the time types. env.ledger().timestamp() is a u64 in seconds, and it is the only clock.

nodes.label: require_auth
nodes.rationale: require_auth asks the host whether this address authorized this contract, this function, and these exact arguments. Require it when the call spends, reduces, reconfigures, or consumes that address's authority downstream. Reads and credits need no auth. Authorizing a caller-supplied who only proves control of who; load the privileged address from storage and authorize that.

nodes.label: require_auth_for_args
nodes.rationale: Narrows the signed payload to the arguments you pass, so a signer can commit to a maximum and the contract enforces actual <= max.

nodes.label: Auth Trees
nodes.rationale: A user signs a tree of invocations, not one call. require_auth passes only if the path and arguments match the signed tree, and each node matches at most once. Auth does not cascade, and SDKs build the tree from simulation. Changing the call graph silently breaks signers of the old shape. Re-authorize at every layer that uses an address's authority. If deposit pulls tokens for a user without user.require_auth, anyone can consume a pre-signed inner transfer. That is the most common real-world auth bug. The host handles replay protection, so contracts do not track nonces.

nodes.label: Medium Threshold
nodes.rationale: Stellar accounts satisfy contract authorization at their medium threshold.

nodes.label: authorize_as_current_contract
nodes.rationale: A direct call from contract A to B authorizes only B's immediate require_auth of A's address. If B will make a deeper call that needs A's auth, A must pre-authorize it with authorize_as_current_contract and an InvokerContractAuthEntry.

nodes.label: __check_auth
nodes.rationale: A contract account (smart wallet, multisig, or passkey) implements CustomAccountInterface. The host calls __check_auth with the signature payload hash, a contracttype signature, and auth contexts. Always verify signature_payload itself. Use auth_contexts for spend limits and allowlists. Never require_auth the account's own address inside __check_auth. Keep it lean; its cost is added to every transaction the account signs. ed25519_verify is the usual signature check.

nodes.label: CAP-71 Auth Delegation
nodes.rationale: Protocol 27 lets __check_auth read get_delegated_signers (unsanitized transaction input; check that each address is a registered delegate) and call delegate_auth to forward the check to a G- or C-address. Delegation can nest, so modular accounts do not need a separate auth entry per delegate.

nodes.label: __constructor
nodes.rationale: Prefer __constructor over a separate initialize. It runs once, atomically, at creation and removes the front-running window between deploy and init. It does not run on upgrade. Failure aborts deployment. A contract deployed without a constructor cannot gain one later.

nodes.label: contractimport
nodes.rationale: Import another contract's WASM to get a typed client. Callee errors abort the caller unless the call goes through a try_ client method.

nodes.label: TokenClient
nodes.rationale: SDK client for the standard token interface, including every Stellar asset through its SAC, so no WASM import is needed. There is no msg.sender: pass the acting Address and require_auth it.

nodes.label: invoke_contract
nodes.rationale: env.invoke_contract is the untyped dynamic call when the interface is not known at compile time.

nodes.label: contractevent
nodes.rationale: #[contractevent] replaces deprecated env.events().publish. The snake-cased name is the first topic unless topics= overrides it; #[topic] fields follow. data_format is map by default, or vec, or single-value (SEP-41 token events). Topics are how indexers filter. Events are cheaper than queryable storage but RPC providers typically keep them about 7 days, so long-term data must be recoverable from state. log! diagnostics are off by default and are not consensus.

nodes.label: contracterror
nodes.rationale: #[contracterror] codes are public ABI and must never be renumbered. foo() panics on error; try_foo() returns Result<Result<T, E>, InvokeError>, where the inner Err is the typed error and the outer Err is a host failure (budget, auth, type mismatch). Use panic_with_error! rather than a bare panic, which clients cannot match. Err or panic rolls back the whole invocation, including nested writes.

nodes.label: panic_with_error!
nodes.rationale: panic_with_error!(&env, Error::X) surfaces a typed error. A bare panic becomes an opaque host error.

nodes.label: SEP-41
nodes.rationale: SEP-41 is the token interface. transfer, approve, and burn authorize from; transfer_from and burn_from authorize the spender. Reads need no auth. mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust are SAC admin operations, not SEP-41.

nodes.label: Stellar Asset Contract
nodes.rationale: Every classic Stellar asset exposes SEP-41 through its SAC, so a token address may be a custom contract, a wrapped classic asset, or native XLM. G-address balances live in trustlines (64-bit cap; missing or unauthorized trustline fails the transfer). C-address balances live in contract storage at full i128 range. Transfers to the issuer burn; transfers from the issuer mint.

nodes.label: StellarAssetClient
nodes.rationale: Admin client for a SAC: mint, clawback, set_admin, set_authorized, and trust (protocol 26+).

nodes.label: Classic Issuer Flags
nodes.rationale: AUTH_REQUIRED, freezes via AUTH_REVOCABLE, and clawback apply to SAC transfers. A protocol that accepts arbitrary token addresses has to survive them.

nodes.label: Token Allowances
nodes.rationale: approve(from, spender, amount, expiration_ledger) expires. The convention is temporary storage keyed by (from, spender) with TTL matching the expiration. Re-approving overwrites, so a spender can front-run a reduction and spend the old amount plus the new one. Approve to 0 first, or use exact-amount auth instead of a standing allowance.

nodes.label: soroban-token-sdk
nodes.rationale: Ships the standard token event shapes as #[contractevent] structs. Wallets and indexers depend on transfer, approve, mint, burn, and clawback using those exact topics and data.

nodes.label: SEP-0011
nodes.rationale: The SAC adds the SEP-0011 asset string (CODE:ISSUER or native) as a trailing topic on the standard token events.

nodes.label: Contract Upgrade
nodes.rationale: If the contract is mutable, gate upgrade on admin or governance auth. Upload the new WASM first and pass its hash to deployer().update_current_contract_wasm. The address and storage survive; only the executable changes, and __constructor does not re-run. A changed #[contracttype] shape fails to decode. Store a schema version, add enum variants instead of reshaping keys, and ship an idempotent admin-gated migrate that requires new_version > current_version. contractmeta! can record binver.

nodes.label: SEP-0049
nodes.rationale: SEP-0049 standardizes upgradeable-contract interfaces.

nodes.label: OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts
nodes.rationale: Ships audited implementations of the upgradeable interfaces standardized by SEP-0049.

nodes.label: Contract Factory
nodes.rationale: deploy_v2 with with_address(current contract, salt) makes the address deterministic per deployer and salt. deployed_address computes it without deploying. Authorize deployers, emit an event per deployment, and keep factory logic out of instance logic.

nodes.label: Governance Timelock
nodes.rationale: For upgrades and config changes, propose stores the action and an execute-after ledger, execute enforces the delay, and cancel lets governance abort. Separate proposer, approver, and executor for multisig, store proposals in persistent storage, and block replay with unique ids, expiry, and events. A custom account is often cleaner than in-contract multisig for signature-set policies.

nodes.label: Vaults
nodes.rationale: Track total_assets and total_shares, round conservatively on mint and redeem, and include pause controls.

nodes.label: Pools and AMMs
nodes.rationale: Define the invariant and fee accounting precisely, and slippage-check every user-facing swap.

nodes.label: Oracles
nodes.rationale: Enforce freshness bounds, prefer multi-source or median feeds, and add circuit breakers.

nodes.label: Regulated Tokens
nodes.rationale: Put allowlist, denylist, freeze, and forced-transfer logic in dedicated entrypoints with strong auth. Emit policy-decision events. Never store PII on-chain.

nodes.label: Resource Limits
nodes.rationale: Transactions pay an inclusion fee plus a resource fee for declared CPU, ledger reads and writes, transaction size, events, and rent. Rent and events are refunded if unused; instructions and I/O are charged as declared, so simulate first and leave headroom when state can diverge from simulation. Mainnet ceilings at time of writing include 400M CPU instructions, 40 MB memory, 200 entries read and 200 written, 200 KB read and about 129 KB written, about 129 KB transaction size, 16 KB events plus return value, 128 KB WASM, and 64 KB per ledger entry (keys 250 bytes). Limits change by validator vote.

nodes.label: Protocol 23
nodes.rationale: Protocol 23 is when archived persistent entries in the footprint started restoring automatically.

nodes.label: Protocol 26
nodes.rationale: Protocol 26 added bounded TTL extension, checked U256/I256 math, and SAC trust.

nodes.label: Contract Size
nodes.rationale: The 128KB limit is real. The release profile is mandatory, and stellar contract build optimizes WASM by default. If the binary is still too big, use cargo-bloat, drop heavy crates such as full serde and regex, split the contract, and avoid large static data.
